name: How much should I budget for home renovation planning fees?

mainEntity.name: What should homeowners budget for design, plans, and permit-related planning fees in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What should homeowners budget for design, plans, and permit-related planning fees in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners planning a renovation in Los Angeles should budget separately for pre-construction services, not just construction itself. Planning costs may include concept design, measured drawings, architectural drafting, structural engineering, energy-related documentation, permit expediting, and city correction responses. Smaller interior remodels may need only a limited planning budget, but larger renovations often require several thousand dollars or more before construction begins. The exact number depends on scope, how many disciplines are involved, and whether the home has unusual conditions such as hillside grading, old framing, or prior unpermitted work. A luxury remodel or whole-home renovation often needs a much more detailed planning phase because mistakes in documents can create costly delays later. Homeowners should ask for a clear breakdown of what is included: design revisions, permit drawings, engineering coordination, and post-submittal corrections. The cheapest planning package is rarely the best value if it produces incomplete plans or repeated review cycles.
acceptedAnswer.description: Planning fees vary widely, but homeowners should budget for design, drafting, engineering, and permit-related costs before construction starts. Small remodels may only need a modest planning budget, while larger renovations can require several thousand dollars or more for architectural plans, structural engineering, and city submittal support.
